A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Chain-of-Zoom work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original DIV2K/DIV8K experiments, prompt and backbone comparisons, and a 25-participant user study in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, an alternative-critic experiment, runtime measurements, and an overlapping-region analysis.

M1.justification: Appendix H adds an explicit full-image inference extension using tiled VAE encoding, overlapping latent patches, patch-specific prompts, and Gaussian-weighted stitching. v1 only states that whole-image outputs require multiple CoZ runs. The core scale-autoregressive procedure, GRPO rewards, and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The training and benchmark datasets remain LSDIR/FFHQ and DIV2K/DIV8K. Appendix G adds a spatial-consistency scenario comparing zooms into overlapping and non-overlapping regions, extending the original center-crop evaluations without introducing a new dataset or domain.

E2.justification: v3 Table 2 adds evaluated comparisons with LIIF, SeeSR, and S3Diff, including S3Diff versus S3Diff plus CoZ. These methods were absent from v1's reported comparisons, which used nearest-neighbor interpolation, direct SR, and CoZ prompt variants. The original comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include timing over 500 DIV2K images with separate SR and prompt-extraction measurements, and a 500-image cosine-similarity test using 50% overlapping patches and non-overlapping controls. Appendix F additionally substitutes Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct for InternVL2.5-8B as critic while explicitly retaining other settings. Existing benchmark preprocessing and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds critic-choice robustness evidence in Figure 7 and Table 5, runtime decomposition in Section 4.4/Table 3, and spatial-consistency/error-accumulation analysis in Appendix G/Table 6. These substantially extend the retained prompt comparisons, user study, backbone-transfer experiment, and failure examples.

E5.justification: Appendix D retains the same participant count, standard-deviation bars, and pairwise t-tests. No new seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or uncertainty-estimation methods are reported. The added tables provide point estimates and descriptive summaries rather than additional uncertainty analysis.

E6.justification: Table 1 and v1's OSEDiff Table 2, now Table 4, retain all numerical entries. v3 adds baseline, runtime, alternative-critic, and overlap results. For example, new Table 2 reports 256× DIV2K NIQE of 16.7809 for S3Diff and 10.7668 for S3Diff plus CoZ. Table 6 also introduces invalid cosine values above 1, limiting interpretation of that analysis.

T1.justification: Proposition 1/Eq. (5) replaces the initial factor p(x0, x1) with p(x0, c1, x1). Eq. (6) correspondingly introduces Linit and starts subsequent sums at i=2; Appendix A revises the integration and indexing. This corrects the treatment of the initial latent variable within the existing derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: model-agnostic scale autoregression, multi-scale VLM prompts, GRPO preference alignment, and extreme magnification without retraining the SR backbone. Added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets alternative-critic results as evidence of robustness and asserts high consistency between overlapping zoom regions. Appendix H newly identifies repeated VLM calls as a computational bottleneck for full-image SR. The original error-accumulation and potential-misuse limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds project-page access information, identifies SWIFT as the fine-tuning infrastructure, and documents full-image tiling with 64×64 latent patches, overlap of 16, and Gaussian blending. Existing hardware, LoRA parameters, training budgets, prompts, and checkpoint access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to LIIF and SWIFT for the new comparison and implementation disclosure. The related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged. SeeSR and the work cited as S3Diff were already referenced in v1; their new evaluation is a separate comparison change.

P1.justification: There are limited grammar and caption edits, an added runtime subsection, acknowledgments, and new Appendices F–H. Most existing prose and section organization are retained, including the conclusion. Original Appendices F and G survive as I and J.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the quantitative displays with baseline, runtime, alternative-critic, and overlap Tables 2, 3, 5, and 6, plus the second-critic reward Figure 7. The original reward plot is relocated, while existing qualitative images and user-study graphics are retained and renumbered where necessary.

improvement.justification: The added external comparisons, critic experiment, runtime breakdown, and corrected initialization derivation strengthen empirical support and technical clarity relative to v1. Implementation disclosures also improve reproducibility. These gains are partly offset by new Table 6, whose printed cosine similarities above 1, including 5.5208, cannot support its spatial-consistency conclusion. The reliable additions therefore yield a limited net improvement.
